headline: OpenAI Releases LifeSciBench, a 750-Task Benchmark Grading AI Models on Real Life-Science Research With Expert-Written Rubric
context: OpenAI's LifeSciBench evaluates whether frontier AI can handle real life-science research across 750 expert-authored tasks, seven workflows, and seven biological domains. Built by 173 PhD scientists with 19,020 rubric criteria, it grades reasoning and decisions, not just recall.

sources.name: MarkTechPost
sources.summary: OpenAI's LifeSciBench evaluates whether frontier AI can handle real life-science research across 750 expert-authored tasks, seven workflows, and seven biological domains. Built by 173 PhD scientists with 19,020 rubric criteria, it grades reasoning and decisions, not just recall. The best model, GPT-Rosalind, passes 36.1%, leaving large headroom on artifacts, exact outputs, and operational calls. The post OpenAI Releases LifeSciBench, a 750-Task Benchmark Grading AI Models on Real Life-Science Research With Expert-Written Rubric appeared first on MarkTechPost .
